jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on the Governance team, you will help build the platform that gives VTEX visibility and control over cost, compliance, and reliability. You will build APIs, dashboards, and automations on the Backstage platform so that product teams can see what they spend, understand why, and act on it without waiting for manual requests. Increasingly, that means building AI agents that spot problems, explain them, and help fix them.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Build governance tooling: Design and build services and APIs for cost metrics, tag compliance, and optimization opportunities.

• Build automation and agents: Ship automations and agents that detect issues, find root causes, and propose or apply fixes, with humans in the loop where it matters.

• Build for developer experience: Create self-service views and workflows that make cost and compliance data easy to understand and act on.

• Work with data: Turn cloud cost and usage data (AWS, Kubernetes) into reliable metrics and reports that people and agents can trust.

• Eliminate toil: Replace manual tracking and follow-ups with automation and alerts.
Support reliability: Help the company prepare for peak events like Black Friday, and take part in incident follow-ups.

WHO YOU ARE

• Solid engineer: You have a good foundation in software engineering and care about clean, tested, maintainable code.

• Curious about cloud and cost: You enjoy understanding how systems run and what they cost. FinOps experience is a plus, not a requirement.

• Product-minded: Your users are other developers, and you build things they actually want to use.

• Data-oriented: You are comfortable working with metrics, APIs and databases.

• AI-builder: You use AI every day to move faster, and you have built with LLMs (tool use, agents, MCP) or are eager to, while staying thoughtful about responsible use.

• Global Communicator: Fluent English; you are capable of collaborating effectively in a fast-paced global environment.

#LI-Remote

About VTEX

VTEX (NYSE: VTEX) is the backbone for connected commerce that delivers more efficiency and less maintenance to organizations seeking to make smarter IT investments and modernize their tech stack. VTEX’s platform is designed to be the AI-native operating system for the commerce ecosystem, enabling enterprise brands and retailers to orchestrate their complex network of consumers, business partners, suppliers, and fulfillment providers in one place. VTEX puts its customers’ business on a fast path to growth with a complete Commerce, Marketplace, and OMS solution. VTEX helps global companies build, manage and deliver native and advanced B2B, B2C, and Marketplace commerce experiences, as well as Retail Media solutions, with competitive time-to-market and without complexity, so they can stay relevant for the modern, convenience-driven consumer. Trusted by 2,200 global B2C and B2B customers, including Carrefour, Colgate, Sony, Stanley Black & Decker, and Whirlpool, VTEX supports 3,100 active online stores across 44

countries (FY ended December 31, 2025).

Founded in the year 2000, VTEX has a history of being unstoppable. Completely against the odds, VTEX is leading a high-tech industry and positioned above market giants. We are building an extraordinary future with more than 1,300 employees scattered across 25 locations in 16 countries in Latin America, North America, Europe, and Asia. For more information, visit www.vtex.com .

At VTEX, you will work in a challenge-driven environment and collaborate with amazing peers. If you are powerful individually, join us, and we will be unstoppable together.

BENEFITS

• Annual profit-sharing program and equity eligibility;

• Health, dental, and life insurance with national coverage provided by VTEX;

• Annual budget for professional development in Tech;

• Language development incentive program (English, Spanish, Portuguese);

• Flexible meal allowance;

• Extended parental leaves;

• Child-care assistance;

• Flexible work schedule and remote-first culture;

• Financial assistance to build your work-from-home setup;

• Wellness program;

• Free shipping on 1000+ VTEX stores

jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Partner

Remote | Latin America | Less than 10% travel

Build the team behind our growth in Latin America

Precision for Medicine is expanding across Latin America, building the people and capabilities needed to support clinical research across key markets including Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, and Peru. Our goal is clear: build strong local teams that allow us to support clients more directly as their programs progress through the drug development lifecycle.

We are looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner who wants to help build that future.

This is more than a traditional recruiting role. You will help shape our talent strategy and employer presence across a region where Precision continues to invest and grow. You will recruit the people who will deliver clinical programs, strengthen our regional capabilities, and help us deliver on the commitments we make to our clients and, ultimately, the patients their therapies are designed to serve.

You will join an established global life sciences organization while working in a region that still offers the opportunity to build, influence, and make your mark.

What you’ll do

• Lead full-cycle recruitment across assigned business areas, from intake and sourcing through interviews, offers, references, and onboarding handoff.

• Partner with hiring managers and business leaders to understand their needs and turn them into focused recruiting strategies.

• Build proactive talent pipelines for specialized and hard-to-fill roles across Latin America.

• Identify and engage passive talent through LinkedIn, professional networks, referrals, market mapping, social channels, and creative sourcing.

• Bring market intelligence to the conversation, including talent availability, competitor activity, compensation trends, and hiring challenges.

• Use recruiting data and insights to identify risks, measure progress, and help leaders make better hiring decisions.

• Create a candidate experience that is transparent, respectful, responsive, and representative of Precision.

• Help strengthen Precision’s employer brand and talent communities across Latin America.

• Partner with regional and global colleagues to improve recruiting processes and build scalable talent acquisition capabilities.

What you bring

• 3+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience in a growing, technical, scientific, or specialized organization.

• Strong sourcing skills and experience building pipelines in competitive talent markets.

• The confidence to advise and influence hiring managers and senior leaders.

• Strong business judgment, ownership, and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Experience using recruiting data and market insights to guide decisions.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• A collaborative, curious, and candid working style.

• Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.

Experience recruiting within life sciences, clinical research, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare, or a CRO environment is preferred. Experience supporting multiple countries or regional hiring is also valuable.

Why Precision?

Latin America represents an important part of Precision’s growth strategy. The region offers experienced clinical research professionals, expanding research infrastructure, diverse patient populations, and the opportunity to strengthen our capabilities in areas where Precision has deep expertise, including oncology, rare disease, and complex clinical development.

You will help us build the teams behind that strategy.

You will have the opportunity to influence how we attract talent, build our presence, and establish Precision as an employer of choice across Latin America.

And the people you recruit will help us do something bigger: support our clients in advancing new therapies through clinical development and closer to the patients who need them.

Ready to help build what comes next?

Apply and help us grow Precision in Latin America.

jobs.title: Sr. Clinical Research Associate (Brazil)
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
Alimentiv is a global CRO with a singular focus: advancing therapies for patients with gastrointestinal diseases. GI is our WHY and for more than 30 years that purpose has driven our scientific rigour, operational excellence, and deep therapeutic expertise, including supporting more than 70% of IBD compounds in development.
We operate as a private, profit-with-purpose company, channeling our commercial success back into scientific research, technology, and our people. With approximately 700 people across multiple countries and three service lines, we are growing deliberately, and the capability of our leaders and our organization is central to how we get there.

If you want to do meaningful work, build something real, and invest back in research that changes lives — we want to meet you!

Job Overview

The Senior Clinical Research Associate (Sr. CRA) independently performs, coordinates and oversees clinical site monitoring activities, ensuring compliance with study protocols, Alimentiv and sponsor procedures, ICH-GCP guidelines and local regulatory requirements.

Serving as a primary liaison between investigative sites, Alimentiv and sponsors, the Sr. CRA plays a key role in the successful execution of clinical studies from site selection and start-up through monitoring and close-out. This role also provides guidance and mentorship to CRA I and CRA II colleagues and may participate in CRA assessment visits, co-monitoring activities, audits and inspections.

Key Responsibilities

•
Independently conduct and document onsite and remote site management activities, including site qualification, initiation, monitoring and close-out visits, in accordance with applicable SOPs and study requirements.

•
Serve as a primary point of contact for investigative sites, building effective working relationships and ensuring site questions, issues, action items and protocol deviations are followed through to resolution.

•
Review source documentation and study systems to ensure clinical data is accurate, complete and compliant with protocol, regulatory and study requirements; manage and facilitate the resolution of data queries.

•
Oversee site activation and ongoing site management activities, working with sites and cross-functional teams to achieve project timelines, milestones and recruitment objectives.

•
Ensure site personnel are appropriately trained on study protocols, plans, systems, ICH-GCP requirements and project-specific expectations.

•
Routinely review Investigator Site Files (ISF), Trial Master Files (TMF) and study systems for accuracy, completeness, timeliness and compliance, requesting outstanding documentation as required.

•
Coordinate site-related study activities and communications, including clinical supplies, investigational product, laboratory materials, ePROs, study documentation and ongoing project updates.

•
Collaborate with Study Start-up, Regulatory and other cross-functional teams, including supporting document collection, localisation and translation activities where required.

•
Participate in study meetings, Investigator Meetings, audits and inspections, supporting issue resolution and implementation of corrective actions when required.

•
Mentor and support CRA I and CRA II colleagues, including CRA Assessment Visits, co-monitoring and sign-off activities; contribute to CRA interviews, training and process improvement initiatives as requested.

Skills & Qualifications

•
(Honours) Bachelor’s degree required; a degree in Health Sciences, Life Sciences, Pharmacy or Nursing is preferred. A Master’s degree is considered an asset.

•
Minimum 4–6 years of relevant clinical research experience; 7–9 years of related experience is preferred.

• Must have previous GI experience.

•
Experience across Phase I–IV clinical trials is preferred.

•
Thorough knowledge of ICH-GCP and applicable local regulatory requirements.

•
Demonstrated experience independently conducting site qualification, initiation, monitoring and close-out visits.

•
Proficiency with clinical trial systems including EDC platforms (e.g., Medidata Rave, Oracle InForm), IRT, eTMF and CTMS, as well as Microsoft Office.

•
Strong interpersonal, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively within cross-functional teams.

•
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage priorities with an appropriate sense of urgency.

•
Fluent written and verbal English; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

•
Valid driver’s licence and ability to travel approximately 40–60%, depending on project assignment and the geographic location of investigative sites.

What We Offer

In addition, as an Alimentiv Employee, you’re also eligible for the following programs:

• Education Reimbursement program for full-time employees

• Monthly Cell Phone and Remote Work Allowance (dependent on role eligibility)

• One time office setup allowance

We're looking for a Senior Analytics Specialist to head up ongoing analytics projects and help build analytical products people trust. You’re the analytical partner our product teams count on, from helping craft the analytics behind a solution’s value (strengthening internal product analytics and ROI storytelling) to refining the product vision and the details of a new analytical product for execution. Product brings the user, the problem, and the direction; you own what it takes to answer it well: defining the right metrics, shaping a coherent story and visualization design, and bringing the rigor that makes people trust the result.

From there, you translate that into the technical substance that gets built: context-rich metric definitions, dashboard requirements, and the validation that makes it hold up, so product leadership can stand behind the results rather than just present them. • Lead analytics projects as their technical owner: scoping key initiatives, running sprints, ticketing, leading project management for the pod, and holding the bar for what ships while keeping things unblocked.

• Own analytical quality for your pod, setting the bar for rigor and correctness, catching flawed definitions and misleading framings before they reach a customer, and holding ultimate technical responsibility for what the pod ships

• Bring analytical rigor into early product discovery, supporting the exploratory analysis and POCs that pressure-test ROI stories and surface what is really provable before the team commits to building

What We're Looking For:

• Sharp, experienced analytical thinking, with a track record of building out high-quality, narratively complete analytical components, not just running ad hoc analyses

• Versatile critical thinking, with demonstrated ability to ramp up quickly and translate general skills into tactical enablement, even without deep domain expertise

• Hands-on expertise with SQL and modern data warehouses (DBX preferred): deep enough to run analysis, support and debug metric definitions, and set the technical standard for your pod.

• Strong data visualization design & BI development skills (Sigma or similar)

• Demonstrated ability to partner with PMs as a trusted peer, turning rough ideas into defensible products and pushing on the thinking without friction

• Experience leading delivery for a small team: comfortable owning sprints, sequencing, and coordination, and getting good work out of a pod without becoming the bottleneck

It's a Plus if You Have…

• Experience leading dashboard development end to end, from design through validation and including hands-on build

• Expertise in the healthcare domain and familiarity with healthcare operational data, clinical workflows, hospital operations, or common healthcare measurement challenges

• Familiarity with data governance, metric governance, or semantic layer concepts, especially where consistency across teams, solutions, or customer implementations is critical

• Deeper technical expertise with hands-on data modeling and transformation experience and standards setting (dbt preferred)

• Experience contributing to analytics QA processes, validation workflows, peer review practices, or release readiness checks for customer-facing analytics

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About TRM

TRM Labs is on a mission to build a safer world by fighting crime and protecting the people who investigate it. We started as a blockchain intelligence company, helping law enforcement, government agencies, financial institutions, and businesses detect, investigate, and disrupt crypto-enabled crime. Today our platform reaches well beyond the blockchain: we fuse on-chain data with cyber and open-source intelligence (OSINT) so investigators can move from a single crypto address to the full story behind a criminal network. Our blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms turn fragmented signals into fast, defensible investigative leads for the teams protecting public safety and national security every day.

TRM Academy delivers training and certification for the global community of investigators, analysts, and compliance professionals who detect and prevent fraud and financial crime involving cryptocurrencies. Learners get live and virtual courses, practical exercises, and a community of the world's experts in blockchain, crypto compliance, and financial crime investigations.

About the Role

As the Lead Instructor, EMEA , you will own the design and delivery of TRM Academy training across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, with blockchain intelligence and crypto investigations at the core of what you teach. You will turn complex on-chain concepts into practical, mission-ready skills for law enforcement, national security, and government audiences, and you will be equally comfortable teaching crypto businesses, exchanges, and financial institutions. Cyber and OSINT tradecraft is the complement: you will show investigators how to pair it with on-chain tracing to build a complete case.

EMEA is a region where we win by showing up. You will deliver in person, in the room, with customers across the UK, DACH, the Nordics and Baltics, France, and beyond, and you will work closely with our regional sales, value engineering, and customer success teams so that training drives adoption and opens the next conversation. You will join a Training Team of master instructors who can command a room, build engaging content, and speak to every level of expertise. We know how our products are used in the real world and help our customers become humble masters too.

This is also a build role. EMEA training is a growing opportunity, and you will help shape how it is scoped, packaged, and delivered as the region scales.

Please note: this role requires travel of 50-75%, primarily across EMEA.

The Impact You'll Have Here

•
Program manage and deliver live, in-person, and virtual blockchain intelligence training to law enforcement, national security, and government learners across EMEA.

•
Teach crypto fundamentals through advanced investigations on TRM's blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms, helping investigators trace funds and build complete, defensible cases.

•
Develop and maintain curriculum, labs, and practical exercises that stay current with the crypto threat landscape, including fraud, scams, ransomware, hacks and exploits, terrorism finance, sanctions evasion, and money laundering typologies.

Adapt content for regional legal frameworks, case types, and audience maturity, from first-time crypto investigators to experienced national security analysts.

Pair on-chain tracing with cyber and OSINT techniques in courses and case walkthroughs, so learners can pivot from off-chain signals to blockchain activity.

•
Partner with sales, value engineering, and customer success to scope training engagements, support onboarding and enablement, and turn training into adoption and expansion.

•
Build relationships with law enforcement and industry partners across the region to grow the TRM Academy cadre and learner community.

3-5+ years of experience instructing courses, leading trainings, or delivering technical instruction.

Blockchain, cryptocurrency, or digital assets subject matter expertise (core requirement), ideally from hands-on on-chain investigations or crypto-enabled crime casework.

Law enforcement or government experience, or a proven track record training these audiences. Police and financial crime investigators are especially welcome.

Experience building coursework, curriculum, labs, and appropriate testing.

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland.

The Opportunity

About our platform

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.

The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads.

About the Infrastructure group

We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.

You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.

We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen.

How we work

Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on.

Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

Responsibilities

• Build the lifecycle communication program end-to-end across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, from strategy through copy, build, launch, and iteration

• Create programs that serve the full customer base while working hardest for digital-only customers, and decide where messaging should differ for accounts with a dedicated team

About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Money

The Money Team owns the financial infrastructure that underpins every dollar and crypto asset that moves through Gemini. We build and operate the ledger platform — the system of record for all crypto and fiat balances, settlements, fees, rewards, and administrative adjustments — as well as the payments services and reconciliation pipelines that connect Gemini to banks, payment rails, and external partners.

Our systems are relied upon by finance, compliance, treasury, and regulatory reporting. Correctness is non-negotiable. If something is ambiguous, we clarify it. If something is manual, we automate it. If something is unsafe, we fix it.

The Role: Senior Software Engineer

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join a team of ledger and financial infrastructure engineers designing, building, and operating core money-movement systems at scale. You'll work on services that must handle high transaction volumes, evolve safely as new products and partners are introduced, and remain easy to operate and audit.

Responsibilities:

• Design, develop, deploy, and support ledger and payments services that accurately record all crypto and fiat money movement across the platform.

• Build and evolve bank settlement and reconciliation pipelines that connect Gemini to external payment rails and banking partners.

• Apply sound engineering principles to identify correctness, consistency, and operational risks — and implement safeguards in software before they become incidents.

• Partner with finance, reconciliation, and treasury teams to understand real-world workflows and translate them into robust, auditable system behavior.

• Design scalable APIs and data models that support new transaction types, products, and regulatory requirements without increasing operational burden.

• Write well-tested, production-grade code that other critical systems depend on.

• Monitor and communicate the health of ledger and payment systems, proactively identify issues, and participate in incident response and remediation.

• Mentor teammates to ensure new functionality is correct, auditable, and production-ready.

• Participate in on-call rotations as needed.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Experience with unit testing, integration testing, and CI/CD pipelines.

• Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

• Ability to reason about and debug complex system behavior across services and data stores.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional partners.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience working on ledger systems, accounting platforms, payments infrastructure, or financial transaction processing.

• Familiarity with double-entry bookkeeping, reconciliation processes, audit requirements, or regulatory reporting.

• Experience integrating with external payment rails or banking partners (ACH, wire, card networks).

• Familiarity with workflow orchestration systems (e.g. Temporal, Cadence) for durable, retryable financial processes.

About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

• Product & Value

• Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.

• Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

• Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.

• Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.

• Change & Adoption

• Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.

• Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.

• Executive & Growth

• Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.

• Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.

• Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)

• Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.

Job Title: Marketing and Communications Specialist

Onboarding is required on day one — four hours starting at 9:00 AM (2 hours organizational onboarding + 2 hours systems and tools onboarding) — and will most likely fall during your full-time job's business hours. Onboarding hours are paid. If you are unable to take off during business hours, this is not the job for you.

Compensation: $32/hr

About Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM)

Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM) is a fast-growing, fully remote mental health practice dedicated to providing evidence-based mental health services to children, adults, and families across multiple states. Our mission is to expand equitable access to mental health services through high-quality virtual care — and to support the clinicians and professionals who make that care possible.

We're building a culture that is mission-driven, accountable, supportive, and built for sustainable remote work.

Why Join VPM

At VPM, you'll be part of a team transforming access to mental health care through virtual care — with a remote model designed to support excellent work and real life.

What you can expect:

• Mission-Driven Impact: Contribute to meaningful work improving access and outcomes for youth and families.

• Remote by Design: Fully remote environment with clear expectations and supportive infrastructure.

• Collaborative Culture: Work with a multidisciplinary team that values integrity, empathy, and shared learning.

• Growth & Leadership Pathways: Opportunities to expand scope and take on leadership or consulting responsibilities as we scale.

• Professional Development: Access to training, resources, and continued learning opportunities aligned to role scope.

• State & School-Based Partnerships: Join initiatives that strengthen school-based mental health delivery and expand access across communities.

Role Overview

VPM is seeking a Marketing and Communications Specialist to tell VPM's story and keep our message consistent everywhere families, schools, and partners see us. This role owns our social media presence, creates and updates marketing materials, supports community outreach events, keeps our website and communications current, and builds the marketing funnels and automated follow-ups that turn interest from families and schools into next steps.

This is a part-time, remote role based in Virginia, with occasional travel to community events. The Marketing and Communications Specialist works closely with the CEO and the Director of Community Engagement and Partnership to make sure everything VPM puts out — from a flyer at a school event to a post on social media — reflects who we are and the care we provide. This is an organization-wide role supporting VPM's private practice, school-based programs, and other approved initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are seeking someone who:

• Writes clearly and well — they can turn an idea into a post, a flyer, or an email without a lot of back-and-forth.

• Is organized and can manage multiple projects and deadlines at once.

• Is self-directed — they see what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be told.

• Values consistency — they care that the logo, the colors, and the message look right every time.

• Understands the mission — they care about access to mental health care and want their work to mean something.

• Is comfortable with feedback and revisions — they don't take edits personally.

• Comfortable with technology and marketing automation — they like building systems that follow up while they focus on the creative work.

• Is looking for a home, not another stop — they want to settle in and grow with the practice.

Who This Role Is Not For

This role may not be the right fit for someone who:

• Needs constant direction to get started on a task.

• Struggles to meet deadlines or juggle more than one project at a time.

• Is uncomfortable writing — most of this role is words.

• Wants a purely creative role with no coordination, admin, or follow-through.

• Is looking for a full-time position.

• Uncomfortable with technology or learning new platforms.

• Is not comfortable working independently in a remote setting.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Germany

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Celonis grew up with the private sector: Deutsche Telekom, Mercedes-Benz, Uniper and three quarters of the DAX companies rely on Celonis Process Intelligence. Now we are taking the next big step in Germany: scaling our business with the public sector. To make this happen, Celonis is investing heavily through 2029 in its German public sector business.

Over the past year, we have built our Public Sector team from the ground up. Today, a strong go-to-market core team of Account Executives and Value Engineers is in place, working with federal and state-level institutions.

The police are one of our primary target organizations in the public sector. Police officers spend a large proportion of their time on data work and comparatively little on the actual investigation. We want to turn that around. With our new police solution, Metropolis, we help police authorities connect and make sense of their data, so that officers can focus on what matters most: solving cases and keeping people safe .

To address this, we are now complementing our existing Public Sector team with a highly specialized Account Executive who brings first-hand experience from inside the organization we serve: the Police .

The Role:

This is not a typical Account Executive role. You bring the perspective of someone who knows police work from the inside: how investigations really run, where time is lost in data work, and how decisions are made and budgets are approved. You will use this credibility to build trusted relationships with police authorities at federal and state level and position Celonis as a long-term partner for their digital transformation.

Working closely with our Public Sector AEs, Value Engineers and product experts, you will translate the operational reality of police work into compelling use cases, contribute to the creation of solution blueprints, drive opportunities from first conversation to signed contract, and help shape how Celonis enters and grows in this market.

The Work you'll do:

• Build and own relationships with police authorities at federal and state level, e.g. Bundespolizei, Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), Landeskriminalämter (LKA), Landespolizeien and the responsible Interior Ministries .

• Engage with decision-makers from police leadership, investigation units, IT and digitalization departments, and procurement

• Translate investigators' daily challenges into concrete, AI-enabled use cases for Celonis and Metropolis, with measurable impact (e.g. time saved per case, faster case processing).

• Bring the voice of the police into Celonis: share insights with our product, marketing and value engineering teams to sharpen our offering.

• Own an individual revenue target and drive complex, long sales cycles to a successful close.

• Navigate public procurement and tender processes (e.g. VgV, VSVgV, UVgO, framework agreements) together with our partners and internal experts.

• Work closely with partners such as consulting firms, system integrators and public IT service providers.

• Represent Celonis at public sector events, conferences and police-specific forums.

The qualifications you need:

• Several years of professional experience within the German police (federal or state level), ideally in a leadership role and/or in an area close to investigations, criminal analysis, IT, digitalization or organizational development.

• A solid network within the police landscape and a deep understanding of how police authorities and Interior Ministries are organized, how decisions are made and how budgets are planned.

• First-hand understanding of the data challenges in police work, e.g. case management, evidence and data analysis, and cross-agency information sharing.

• A strong interest in moving into a commercial, customer-facing role. Prior experience in sales, business development or consulting is a plus, but not a must. We will support your onboarding into the sales role.

We are looking for dependable, detail-oriented Remote Customer Support Specialists to support a US-based affordable housing services operation.
This opportunity involves supporting residents, prospective tenants, and authorized third-party representatives across three key functions: maintenance support, housing locator services, and open-line reporting.

Maintenance Support

We are a small US firm that writes federal funding proposals for technology companies, for a fixed fee. We are looking for one US-based closer for booked calls. The role starts with a paid two-week trial.

The work

• Our sales are written-first. A prospect replies to our email, receives a free one-page written plan, and picks a call time in writing. You take those booked calls, return calls from prospects who phoned us, and rebook missed calls. No cold dialing and no lists.

• On each call you qualify, present our written fixed-fee offer (mid four figures to low five figures), confirm who signs, and ask for the decision. We send every agreement and payment link.

• You send a short written report after each call, the same day.

• Calls are in US business hours (Eastern Time). The work is remote.

Who fits

• You are based in the United States.

• You have personally closed B2B service sales of US$5,000 or more with business owners or technical founders, on the phone.

• Experience selling to companies that pursue federal, SBIR or defense work is a strong plus.

• You are comfortable following a written call guide and firm rules: no promises about outcomes and no discounts.

• You do not currently write or sell federal proposal, white paper, SBIR or capture services for anyone else.

How we screen and what we pay

• Your written answers to the three questions below.

• Finalists record a 3 to 5 minute drill on a short script we send. The drill is paid: US$40.

• Every drill is scored on the same written scorecard.

• The strongest candidates are offered a paid two-week trial: US$45 an hour, up to 10 hours a week, plus 15% of the fees we actually collect on deals you close. The exact terms are in a written agreement you see before you start.

• The role after the trial depends on results. We do not promise a drill, a trial, a hire, or any number of hours, calls, deals or earnings. Call volume is modest today.

Part-time to start; the best performer moves to more hours as booked calls grow.

To apply, email these three answers. Everything is in writing.

• Describe one B2B service sale of US$5,000 or more that you personally closed: what the service was, the price, and who signed.

• Your city and state, and the hours you could work each week between 9 am and 6 pm Eastern Time.

• A prospect says, "Send me something and I'll think about it." What do you say next? Use your own words.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•

Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.

Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.

You know how to build relationships that matter and understand the US enterprise tech landscape. You enjoy creating spaces where senior leaders actually want to connect and learn. If you’re ready to shape how a major developer brand grows its B2B footprint from the ground up, keep reading.

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do

The US is our largest market, and we already have a strong customer base here. Now, we need to build a more focused, relationship-driven field marketing presence to drive our next phase of B2B growth. You’ll take the lead on shaping this approach from the ground up. Working closely with our US Sales and global marketing teams, you’ll design programs that engage enterprise decision-makers and strengthen strategic customer relationships. You’ll have the autonomy to prioritize target accounts and geographic markets, activating agencies and partners to scale your execution across the country.

Day to day, you will:

• Partner with Sales to map out target accounts, industries, and regional priorities, turning global strategies into focused US programs.

• Design and run executive roundtables, customer events, and industry programs that bring senior technology leaders together.

• Select and manage a network of agencies, event organizers, and partners to help execute your strategy across the US.

• Collaborate with global account-based marketing (ABM) teams to generate qualified leads and build meaningful business opportunities.

• Translate our broader narrative around agentic software development into relevant field initiatives that resonate with enterprise tech leaders.

What you’ll bring

• An entrepreneurial mindset. You are comfortable building programs from scratch and navigating ambiguity.

• A hands-on approach to your work. You take ownership of the strategy while also handling the details.

• Exceptional communication skills. You engage confidently with senior executives and stakeholders.

• A collaborative spirit. You build strong working relationships with global, cross-functional teams across different time zones.

• Deep industry insight. You understand exactly how software engineering organizations evaluate and adopt new technologies.

What you’ll need

• Proven success in US B2B field marketing, ideally within enterprise software or SaaS.

• A track record of attracting senior technology decision-makers to targeted events and account programs.

• Experience coordinating multiple external partners and agencies while maintaining strategic control.

• Practical experience running account-based marketing (ABM) initiatives in close collaboration with sales teams.

• Location in the United States and the ability to travel domestically as needed.

What success looks like

In your first few months, you’ll establish strong alignment with US Sales and global marketing, identifying key regional priorities. Long-term, you’ll build a predictable, high-impact field marketing engine that deepens our relationships with enterprise decision-makers, generates qualified business opportunities, and establishes JetBrains as a trusted partner for AI-driven software development in the US.

Why join JetBrains?

• Strong base salary. We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience.

• Flexible work schedule. Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office.

• Extra time off. More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.

• Learning and development opportunities. Access to conferences, courses, and language classes.

If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

Headquarters: Remote

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Medical Assistant) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8am to 5pm or 9am to 6pm in your local time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision.

• Biased toward action - you bring clinical authority to every interaction, make the call when it counts, and take ownership of outcomes.

What You Need

• An active Medical Assistant certification from an accredited association (either AAMA, AMCA, AMT, NHA, NAHP, NCCT, NRCMA/NRCAMA, or AAH) is required.

• At least 5 years of experience as a Medical Assistant is required.

• Remote work readiness (including stable high-speed WiFi) is required.

• Experience working in internal medicine, cardiology, nephrology or with the geriatric population is pr

Job Title: Senior GTM Engineer

Location: United States, Remote

This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

Revenue is complex, and clarity is rare. Our mission at Salesloft is to transform revenue complexity into clear, decisive action for every team driving growth.

We’re building the industry’s first Predictive Revenue System, where humans and AI work together to make confident decisions based on real signals. Thousands of customers run on our platforms every day, which gives us Revenue Context: a view into what happens in a deal, when, and with what outcome.

Our vision is a future where revenue growth is predictable and the teams driving it are unstoppable. If you want to help build it, alongside people who Move as One and let Evidence over Ego guide the work, we’d love to meet you.

THE OPPORTUNITY
At Salesloft, our Senior GTM Engineer is pivotal to turning signals into pipelines. You will be the first dedicated GTM Engineer on the Marketing Operations & GTM Engineering team, reporting to the Director, Marketing Operations & GTM Engineering, with real ownership and a direct line to the people running the pipeline.

We just brought two companies together and rebuilt our CRM and marketing stack, and now we need someone who builds. You will own the systems that connect our data (Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks) to action (Salesloft Rhythm, Marketo, LeanData), turn buying signals into plays reps actually run, and put AI agents to work on the busywork that slows marketing, sales, and CS down.

On a day-to-day basis, you will be responsible for building and running the GTM systems that drive the pipeline. Specifically, you will:

• Build and maintain integrations and workflows across Salesforce, Salesloft, Clari, Marketo, LeanData, ZoomInfo, 6sense, 1mind, and Tines.

• Write SQL and Python against Snowflake and Databricks to build signal logic, scoring, and data products.

• Turn usage, intent, job change, pipeline-trigger, and deal-health signals into Rhythm plays, and measure what they produce.

• Build and run AI agents and automations with logging, guardrails, and a named owner for each one.

• Keep data clean through deduplication, enrichment waterfalls, field governance, and routing hygiene.

• Partner with Business Systems, Data & Analytics, and RevOps so what you build fits the platform instead of working around it.

• Document everything, so that if you’re out for two weeks, the system keeps running.

HOW YOU’LL WORK HERE (our values, in this role)

• Move as One: You’ll partner with Business Systems, Data & Analytics, and RevOps so what you build fits the platform instead of working around it.

• Evidence over Ego: You’ll measure what your plays produce and retire the signals that don’t perform.

• Lead from the Front: You’ll own the systems you build from launch through monitoring, with a named owner for each one, and document them so they keep running when you’re out.

• Make Your Mark: As the first dedicated GTM Engineer on the team, you’ll shape how we turn signals into pipelines and help hire the next GTM Engineer.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
You’re a bias-towards-action, results-oriented builder who ships production systems, explains them to a sales leader in plain English, and stays laser-focused on the pipeline. If you want to learn more, do more, and become more, this is your next move.

YOU’LL BRING

• 5+ years building in GTM systems (RevOps, marketing ops, sales ops, or GTM engineering), with production builds you can walk us through.

• Strong SQL and working Python or JavaScript, and comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, and JSON.

• Hands-on Salesforce experience, plus at least two of: Marketo, LeanData, Salesloft or Outreach, 6sense, ZoomInfo, Snowflake.

• Experience with a workflow or iPaaS tool such as Tines, Tray, Workato, or n8n.

• You’ve shipped something with LLMs or agents that real people rely on every day.

• You can explain a build to a sales leader in plain English and tie it to the pipeline.

IT’S A BONUS IF YOU HAVE

• Experience with dbt, reverse ETL (Census, Hightouch), or Databricks.

• Experience with Clay or ZoomInfo GTM Studio.

• You’ve been through a merger or a CRM migration.

• A background in marketing ops or RevOps before moving into engineering.

THE TEAM
You’ll be the first dedicated GTM Engineer on the Marketing Operations & GTM Engineering team, reporting to the Director, Marketing Operations & GTM Engineering. We just brought two companies together and rebuilt our CRM and marketing stack, so you’ll have real ownership and a direct line to the people running the pipeline. You’ll hear “Yes, let’s do that!” and then have the opportunity to execute on your ideas.

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Licensed Practical Nurse) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

Who You Are

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Remote work readiness (including stable high-speed WiFi) is required.

• An active CA state LVN license is required

• Fluency in Spanish is preferred.

• Experience providing patient ed

ABOUT THE COMPANY:
The company is a Melbourne-based landscape design studio founded by Drew Burns, specialising in native and climate-adaptive gardens for residential clients across Melbourne and the Mornington Peninsula. The client's philosophy is simple: every project starts with a clear plan that resolves layout, levels, materials, and planting before anything is built - so construction happens without guesswork, miscommunication, or costly rework.
The studio's process runs in two stages: a concept report developed locally with the client, followed by detailed construction drawings. We're growing our team to bring the construction drawing stage in-house on an offshore basis, freeing up our local design team to focus on new client work while drawings progress in the background.

ROLE OVERVIEW:
We're looking for a skilled CAD draftsperson to take finalised landscape design concepts and turn them into accurate, buildable construction drawing sets. This is a genuine long-term team role, not a one-off gig - we're investing in someone who wants to grow with the business, not just complete tasks.
The ideal candidate is confident in producing both construction drawings and photorealistic renders, giving us a single point of contact who can carry a project from concept through to construction-ready documentation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Convert approved concept designs into detailed, accurate construction drawing sets (setout plans, levels, sections, details, planting plans, and material schedules).

• Work primarily in Vectorworks to ensure drawings are consistent with the client's existing file standards and templates.

• Produce photorealistic or presentation-quality renders to support client approvals, where required.

• Liaise with Drew and the local design team to clarify design intent, resolve details, and incorporate feedback.

• Maintain drawing accuracy for levels, drainage falls, and material junctions so drawings are genuinely buildable on site.

• Manage your own workflow and deadlines across multiple concurrent projects, flagging risks or delays early.

• Keep drawing files, layers, and naming conventions organised and consistent across projects.

• Proven, verifiable proficiency in Vectorworks is strongly preferred.

• Candidates with strong experience in SketchUp, Revit, or AutoCAD will also be considered - we're open to supporting a transition to Vectorworks.

• Background in landscape architecture, landscape design, or architectural drafting, ideally with residential project experience.

• Understanding of construction documentation: setout, levels, sections, details, and materials - not just drafting for visual presentation.

• Rendering skills (e.g, Enscape, D5) are a strong advantage.

• Strong written English for clear communication with the Australian-based team.

• Reliable internet connection and the ability to work overlapping hours with an Australian (Melbourne, AEST/AEDT) team.

What We're Looking For
Technical skill matters, but it's not the only thing we're hiring for. We value:

• Genuine attention to detail - drawings that are accurate the first time, not just "close enough."

• Strong work ethic and reliability - someone who owns their workload and communicates proactively.

• A long-term mindset - we're looking to invest in this role and grow it over time, not treat it as disposable outsourced labour.

• Honesty about your actual skill level and software experience - we'd rather know upfront than discover gaps later.

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. About the Role

Gusto is looking for a seasoned performance marketer to own execution across paid social and emerging acquisition channels, testing new platforms, formats, and tactics to find what works before scaling. This is a high-visibility role at the intersection of performance marketing, channel experimentation, and AI-powered workflow design. You will own execution and day-to-day strategy for paid social and new channel tests, working within Gusto's demand generation framework, with clear accountability to pipeline and revenue targets.

About the Team

As a member of Gusto's Demand Generation team, you will be embedded specifically within Paid Acquisition, a focused group responsible for driving awareness and pipeline through paid media. This team operates with high autonomy, a bias for experimentation, and a culture of cross-functional partnership. We hold ourselves to a high standard, move fast, and genuinely believe that being AI-native is part of what it means to do this job well today.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day:

• Own paid social strategy and execution across Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, Quora, and TikTok, driving full-funnel campaigns from brand awareness through retargeting and conversion, with accountability to pipeline and revenue targets.

• Manage significant, multi-million dollar budgets with rigor, including campaign pacing, forecasting, budget-vs-actuals analysis, and making the case for paid social investment in imperfect attribution environments.

GrowthBricks is a shared business brain for GTM teams and AI agents.

It brings together the context that usually lives across CRM, docs, dashboards, tools, and people’s heads: who we sell to, why customers buy, what matters now, what we tried, and what worked. Agents and people use that context to decide what to do next and execute across the GTM stack.

You’ll work directly with the product founder and own the technical side of the product: architecture, core systems, integrations, and the agent layer.

The core challenge is turning fragmented, changing business context into reliable memory and agent actions across tools and measuring whether those actions actually drive business outcomes.

You’ll write a lot of the early code yourself, make the key technical decisions, and shape the product as we learn what works.

• Understand how context, prompting, tools, and agent behavior fit together.

• Can design backend systems, APIs, data models, and integrations.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Overview

The Advertiser Optimization team is the decision-making engine of Instacart's $1B+ ads business. We own the systems responsible for Bidding, Pacing, Budgeting, Targeting and advertiser-facing recommendations - converting stated advertiser goals into real-time auction actions. Our mission is to maximize realized Advertiser Value by deciding when to participate, how much to bid, and how fast to spend, all while carefully balancing User Experience and Platform Revenue.

In this role, you will apply your expertise in operational research, mathematics, statistics, economics, or a related field to help build and refine the algorithmic systems that power how Instacart's advertising marketplace operates. • Develop and evaluate models and algorithms for ads bidding, pacing, and budgeting, applying your training in operational research, mathematics, statistics, economics, or a related quantitative discipline to solve complex marketplace problems at scale.

• Collaborate closely with senior scientists, engineers and product managers to translate well-defined marketplace questions into mathematical formulations, implement analyses and prototypes, design experiments, and interpret results using large-scale data.

• Contribute to production systems through algorithm implementation, validation, and monitoring, progressively taking ownership of well-scoped projects from initial hypothesis through measurable impact.

• Operate in a fast-paced, constantly evolving environment where the ads marketplace shifts quickly — you'll need to balance rigor with speed, and thrive when priorities change and new challenges emerge.

• Strong analytical and communication skills, including the ability to explain assumptions, methodologies, results, and limitations to both technical and cross-functional audiences.
